topic: Vecline: Bit-Exact SVG and Document Toolkit for Measurable AI Image Output
keyword: bit exact svg ai image toolkit

key_points: Primary source: the tool's own MIT-licensed repo. Measurable raster⇄SVG conversion covering ten raster formats with measured (not asserted) accuracy.
Bit-exact on flat art: SSIM 1.0000, PSNR inf, zero differing pixels, verified by rendering the SVG back.
Zero-dependency core (vecline/core) that is CI-asserted to bundle for a browser at ~96 KB minified.
Four modes: auto (default), lossless (bit-exact-or-fail), pixel (real editable geometry, bit-exact), trace (Bézier curves, approximate + measured), embed (bitmap in SVG, bit-exact).
--lossless returns bit-exact SVG or errors out; never silently near-miss. Enforced by measurement not construction.
Vecline Studio (vecline.xyz): free, private, in-browser image-to-vector studio. Source-available, not open source.
Everything runs in the tab via a Web Worker — no backend, no upload, no account, works offline once cached.
Measures its own output: renders the SVG it produced and reports real SSIM/PSNR/CIEDE2000 + a bit-exact badge.
Exports SVG, PNG, DXF (with real physical cut size), EPS, PDF, G-code, React/Vue/Svelte/Solid components, colour separations, sprite sheets, favicons, BlurHash.
Handles TGA/PNM/ICO browsers can't read; PDFs via mupdf-WASM; Office documents via vecline serve (local LibreOffice bridge).
Official comparison harness: every tool's SVG rendered with the SAME renderer, scored with the SAME metrics on the same white ground.
Field: potrace, imagetracerjs, and vtracer (VisionCortex, Rust) — the strongest modern open-source rival.
vtracer measured against its own released binary (not the third-party @neplex binding), which is substantially smaller.
Honest trade-offs stated: vecline slower than imagetracerjs (1.10x-1.55x) and 4.08x slower than vtracer on small logos due to Node module load; faster than vtracer on heavier photos.
npm package vecline v2.1.4, MIT license, homepage vecline.xyz, bin 'vecline'. Node.js >=18.17.
Broad keyword surface: svg, vectorize, raster, png-to-svg, jpg-to-svg, svg-to-png, lossless, ssim, psnr, delta-e, bmp, ico, tga, pdf, dxf, gcode, mcp, local-first, privacy, potrace-alternative.
The measured image + document toolkit for JavaScript: bit-exact SVG from flat art, leads potrace/imagetracerjs/vtracer on photos.
Includes an MCP server (vecline mcp) with twelve tools so AI agents/IDEs (Claude, Codex, VS Code, Cursor) can call it directly.
Vecline MCP server officially registered under io.github.shunyagatha/vecline, also on Smithery.
Twelve tools: vectorize, convert, centerline, measure, diff, crop, doc_to_images, office_convert, images_to_pdf, palette, placeholder, image_info.
measure/diff report REAL SSIM/PSNR/CIEDE2000 by rendering the result back and comparing — a model can verify its own output.
All tools openWorldHint:false — nothing touches the network; three read-only, eight destructive (annotated). One-click .mcpb launcher available.

stats.fact: On flat artwork — logos, icons, UI, screenshots, pixel art — Vecline produces bit-exact SVG: SSIM 1.0000, PSNR infinity, zero differing pixels, verified by rendering it back.
On a real logo, Vecline lossless mode returns 24.0 KB at SSIM 1.0000 — about a third of what imagetracerjs (64 KB) and vtracer (60 KB) spend while only approximating.
Vecline 'pixel' mode produces genuine editable vector paths that rasterise back to input with literally zero differing pixels, not 'visually identical'.

On real photographs (Kodak set at 480px), Vecline auto mode leads SSIM on every photo by 0.05-0.18: 0.9140/0.9453/0.8460 vs vtracer's 0.7652/0.7624/0.7949 and imagetracerjs 0.7093/0.7465/0.7615, with far better PSNR (34.8/36.3/31.2 dB vs 25.9/24.3/23.2).

Vecline is slower than imagetracerjs on every fixture (1.10x-1.55x) and 4.08x slower than vtracer on a small logo (280 ms vs 69 ms), but faster in wall clock than vtracer on the two heavier photographs (portrait 1001 ms vs 1386 ms).
Tracing a photograph can never be bit-exact: a photograph holds more independent information than any compact set of Bézier curves can encode. Vecline states this honestly.

Gradient output reconstructs smooth colour ramps (skies, skin) as SVG gradients instead of flat bands: on a synthetic vignette a radial gradient achieves 0.998 SSIM in ~350 bytes where flat bands take 3-8 KB at 0.73-0.88.

Geometric primitives: a plain disc renders as a real <circle> (68% smaller), and a four-slice pie chart goes from 2323 bytes of Bézier to 488 bytes of real arcs — editable as shapes and true arcs for CAD/DXF.
Vecline has an 11x11 = 121-format conversion matrix (every format it reads it writes: PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, TIFF, GIF, BMP, ICO/CUR, PNM, TGA, SVG) run in CI on every commit.
vecline/core, the vectorisation and measurement engine, has zero dependencies and no Node built-ins; CI-asserted to bundle for a browser at ~96 KB minified with a size tripwire.
Vecline collects nothing: no server, no analytics, no telemetry, no account. Every conversion (tracing, measuring, cropping, PDF/Office rendering) runs on the user's own machine.
A photograph can be emitted as exact geometry but costs one rectangle per pixel — a 320x240 photo becomes a 1.99 MB file of 42,933 shapes, so 'auto' uses embed and reports the ratio.

angles: The core differentiating thesis: 'measured, not asserted' — every accuracy claim is verified by rendering the SVG back to pixels and scoring with SSIM/PSNR/CIEDE2000, and --lossless fails rather than silently giving a near-miss.
Bit-exact is the honest 2026 answer to the overhyped '100% accuracy' claims of most vectorizers. Vecline is the tool that makes exact output the default guarantee for logos/icons/UI.

AI-native angle: the built-in MCP server (vecline mcp) lets AI agents verify their own image output rather than asserting it worked — measure and diff report real metrics. Strong for the blog's AI/dev-tooling audience.
Local-first privacy: free, unlimited, no upload, works offline, source-available Studio — a counterpoint to cloud vectorizers that charge per image or upload artwork.

Honest engineering culture: the author publishes measured trade-offs (potrace smaller, vtracer beats it on tuned flags, speed slower than imagetracerjs), even correcting earlier false claims in the changelog.
For makers: DXF at a real physical cut size + EPS + G-code + colour separations make it a full pipeline from raster to laser/CNC/screen-printing, not just a dev tool.
